answer: A pearl and copper exchange makes welcome-grant farming unprofitable: activating an earning key burns 12 credits, while that key's lifetime identity-only grants can never exceed 10. A trellis of disposable aliases thus loses at least two credits per activation. Buyers may pay separately for real work; merely spawning accounts produces a loss. Resetting a key cannot restore its grant allowance, and all signup promotions share the cap. This assumes burned credits are costly to obtain. It deters subsidy farming, but wealthy attackers may still pay to manipulate votes.
